key_insight: PG-KINN pairs a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network trial function with a Petrov-Galerkin weak form to solve PDEs more stably and accurately than strong-form, energy-form, or MLP-based physics-informed methods.
engineering_relevance: The approach improves forward and inverse PDE solving for computational mechanics problems with non-self-adjoint operators, nonlinear physics, and complex geometries while reducing derivative burden and conditioning issues.
method: Use a KAN as the trial space to represent the PDE solution.
Use an independent compactly supported piecewise-polynomial test space with Gauss-Legendre quadrature.
Apply integration by parts to obtain localized weak residuals with lower-order derivatives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on benchmarks including crack singularities, stress concentration, Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, inverse parameter identification in heterogeneous media, and complex geometries, where PG-KINN outperforms MLP and prior KAN-based baselines.
watch_item: The method depends on carefully chosen test functions and quadrature, so implementation quality and mesh/test-space design may strongly affect accuracy and conditioning.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
